questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: When the price of a good changes, the effect on quantity demanded is the result of an income and a substitution effect. Which statement about these effects is always correct?

options.A: For inferior goods, the income effect and substitution effect work in the same direction.
options.B: For inferior goods, the substitution effect outweighs the income effect.
options.C: For normal goods, the income effect and substitution effect work in the same direction.
options.D: For normal goods, the income effect outweighs the substitution effect.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s total product of labour curve. TPL total product of labour O N N N
What could cause a perfectly competitive firm’s marginal revenue product of labour curve to shift to the right?

options.A: an increase in wages
options.B: a higher rate of sales tax
options.C: an increase in labour supply
options.D: a rise in the price of the final product

questions.questionText: A firm currently employs 30 workers at a daily wage of $50. The marginal cost of employing one extra worker is $112 per day. By how much will the firm have to increase the daily wage in order to increase its labour force from 30 to 31 workers?

Which is a risk-bearing economy of scale?

options.A: greater bargaining power in purchasing from suppliers
options.B: greater diversification of the product range
options.C: lower costs in raising capital
options.D: lower distribution costs by increasing market share

questions.questionText: A firm estimates that, all else remaining unchanged, an increase in its output would leave its revenue unchanged. What can be deduced from this about the price elasticity of demand for the firm’s product?

options.A: It is –1.
options.B: It is +1.
options.C: It is perfectly inelastic.
options.D: It is perfectly elastic.

questions.questionText: A firm currently aims to maximise its sales revenue. What is likely to happen if the firm decides instead to aim at maximising profit?

options.A: a reduction in the price of the firm’s product
options.B: a reduction in the price of the firm’s shares
options.C: a reduction in the firm’s market share
options.D: an increase in the number employed by the firm

questions.questionText: In the diagram, DD is the demand curve facing a monopoly producer, and the rectangular hyperbola ATC is the firm’s average total cost curve. D price, cost ATC D

Firms X, Y and Z are profit maximising private firms. X operates in a perfectly competitive industry, Y in a monopolistically competitive industry and Z is a single monopolist. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Only X satisfies the condition for allocative efficiency.
options.B: Only X faces no barriers to entry in the long run.
options.C: Only Y and Z can make a supernormal profit in the long run.
options.D: Only Z is a price maker.

questions.questionText: What would be the short-run effect on price, output and profits of an increase in demand for the product of a monopolistically competitive firm? price output profits

options.A: increase increase increase
options.B: increase no change decrease
options.C: no change increase increase
options.D: no change no change increase

options.D: The country experienced continuous economic growth between 2000 and 2010.

questions.questionText: Which asset would not be included in a country’s broad money supply?

options.A: deposits in commercial banks held for specified minimum periods of time
options.B: deposits in commercial banks transferable by cheque
options.C: deposits in the central bank held by commercial banks
options.D: notes and coins held by private individuals

questions.questionText: Which represents a leakage from an economy’s circular flow of income?

options.A: a government budget surplus
options.B: bank loans to private companies
options.C: foreign direct investment in the economy
options.D: the sale of assets by the country’s households

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between consumption expenditure and income. C consumption O income Which statement is correct?

options.A: The average propensity to consume is falling.
options.B: The average propensity to consume is rising.
options.C: The marginal propensity to consume is rising.
options.D: The marginal propensity to consume is falling.

questions.questionText: A 6% increase in the money supply leads to a 10% increase in the level of money income. What can be deduced from this?

options.A: There has been an increase in the level of output.
options.B: There has been an increase in interest rates.
options.C: There has been an increase in the velocity of circulation.
options.D: The price level has increased by 4%.

questions.questionText: Despite a balance of payments deficit a country’s money supply remains unchanged. What could explain this?

options.A: The country’s foreign exchange rate is fixed.
options.B: The government runs a budget surplus.
options.C: There is a fall in the country’s foreign exchange reserves.
options.D: The government runs a budget deficit financed by borrowing from the central bank.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to lead in the long run to an increase in world real GDP per head?

options.A: faster population growth
options.B: trade liberalisation
options.C: a lower propensity to save
options.D: faster growth of the money supply

questions.questionText: Which government policy would boost economic growth but not necessarily promote economic development?

options.A: creating a more equal distribution of income and wealth
options.B: diverting government spending from industry to education
options.C: encouraging the extraction of finite natural resources
options.D: introducing tighter controls on air pollution

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment is associated with a deficiency in aggregate demand?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: structural
options.D: voluntary

The rate of inflation is currently stable at the central bank’s target rate of 2%. If the central bank’s inflation target is raised from 2% to 5%, what is likely to happen to interest rates and the exchange rate? interest rates exchange rate

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

questions.questionText: Which action is consistent with a policy of ‘trade not aid’?

options.A: abolishing subsidies paid to producers in developed economies
options.B: encouraging the activities in developing countries of non-governmental organisations (NGOs)
options.C: limiting the activities of multinational companies (MNCs) from developed economies
options.D: reducing the size of quotas on imports from developing countries
